standard.title: Base words, prefixes and suffixes
standard.description: understand how to apply knowledge of common base words, prefixes, suffixes and generalisations for adding a suffix to a base word to read and comprehend new multimorphemic words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students build morphemic word families using prefixes and suffixes (AC9E2LY12). They have not yet applied generalisations for adding suffixes to base words (e.g. doubling, dropping 'e').
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply knowledge of base words, prefixes and suffixes to read and comprehend new multimorphemic words.

nodes.label: Prefixes changing base word meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use knowledge of prefixes to change the meaning of a base word and read new multimorphemic words.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the base word and prefix in at least three multimorphemic words, explain how the prefix changes the meaning, and read the words correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Use knowledge of prefixes to change the meaning of base words; read new multimorphemic words by recognising base + prefix structure.
wider: Collect words with the same prefix (e.g. 'un-') and generalise about what the prefix consistently does to meaning
Explore how knowing one prefix helps decode a whole family of unfamiliar words encountered in reading

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a repertoire of common prefixes and their meanings to use morphological knowledge productively as a decoding strategy. Range of examples matters more than depth on a single prefix.

success_criteria: Student identifies the base word and prefix in a multimorphemic word
Student explains how the prefix changes the meaning of the base word

nodes.label: Suffix generalisations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply generalisations for adding a suffix to a base word (doubling, dropping 'e') to form plurals and past tense correctly.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two suffix generalisations correctly (e.g. double the final consonant before '-ing'/'-ed' for CVC words; drop the 'e' before a vowel suffix) and explain the rule applied.
nodes.typical_width: Use generalisations for adding a suffix to form plurals and past tense — including doubling the final consonant and dropping the 'e'; apply to form and read multimorphemic words.
wider: Find exceptions to the doubling rule and discuss why the exceptions exist — exploring what patterns predict when doubling applies
Compare suffix generalisations in English with known patterns in another language if applicable — discussing similarities and differences

response_modes.reason: Suffix generalisations are precision spelling rules that require repeated application in writing before they become automatic. Students know the rules but apply them inconsistently — practice across multiple words is the remedy.

success_criteria: Student correctly applies the doubling or 'drop e' rule when adding a suffix
Student can state the generalisation they applied
